subject: Elliptic Health: deployment pathcheck and GPU sizing checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Park <amy@elliptichealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap: Elliptic throughput & deployment options

Hi Amy — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side: 

Summary of discussion
- Primary objective: move core clinical summarization and triage pipeline to a production inference stack with predictable latency and cost.
- Considered deployment modes: Hosted API (fast onboarding), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput & data isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.

Our read and immediate recommendation
- Given your required 95th percentile latency target (~<=300ms) and the need to process PHI within your VPC, Dedicated is the best starting point. It gives consistent throughput and lets us isolate data paths.
- We also recommend keeping a Hosted fallback route for burst traffic (short-term) while Reserved pool handles steady-state.

Info we need from you to size a Dedicated pool
- Peak TPS (concurrent requests per second) and expected daily request shape (spiky vs steady).
- Typical token mix: avg tokens generated per request, prompt length, 95th pct token lengths.
- Models you plan to run (open Llama-family, fine-tuned instruction variants, embedding-only endpoints).
- Any VPC/KMS restrictions or compliance evidence required for procurement.

Initial asks / attachments
- I've attached a short worksheet (redwood-dedicated-worksheet-v1.xlsx) to capture TPS and token mix — can you fill and return? Also included a CSV example of token distributions.
- Next step: we propose a 2-hour benchmark slot (synthetic + a small sample of your anonymized payloads) to run across two GPU flavors (H100 and A10G) to compare tail latency and tokens/sec.

If you can share peak TPS and avg token counts by end of day tomorrow, we will produce a preliminary GPU mix and a rough cost delta for H100 vs A10G vs L4.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake

jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Elliptic throughput & deployment options

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few data points from our side to get you unstuck: 

- Peak TPS: ~120 TPS sustained for short bursts (5–15m), 60 TPS steady-state through the day.
- Token mix (rough): avg prompt 120 tokens, avg generation 330 tokens => ~450 tokens total per request. 95th pct request ~1,200 tokens.
- Models: plan to run a fine-tuned instruction model for summarization + an embeddings batch job for nightly indexing. The instruction model is roughly MPT-variant tuned by our ML team.
- Security: we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys. SOC2 Type II in place.

Questions for you: 
1) What across-the-board latency should we assume per token on H100 vs A10G vs L4 for a model of this class? Ballpark is fine — we mainly need to decide if H100 is required or a mix will work.
2) Is bursting to your Hosted API from Dedicated possible if we hit larger-than-expected spikes? Any operational caveats?

We can fill the worksheet this afternoon. For procurement: our Purchasing team needs a one-page summary of the proposed configuration and an estimated monthly committed spend range to include in an internal approval.

— Amy

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Elliptic throughput & deployment options — initial sizing thoughts

Thanks Amy — the numbers are super helpful. Based on the token profile and TPS you shared, here are conservative sizing options and answers to your questions: 

Ballpark latency per token (for instruction-like models, unquantized baseline)
- H100 (fp16/optimized kernels): ~0.7–1.0 ms/token median; tail depends on sequence length and KV cache reuse.
- A10G / A10X: ~1.5–2.5 ms/token median for similar models. Good cost/throughput for mid-size workloads.
- L4 (efficient int8 variants): ~2.0–3.5 ms/token median but much cheaper for embedding-only or trimmed models.

Recommended Dedicated pool (initial) — conservative sizing for 120 TPS peak, 450 token avg:
- Option A (latency-first): 4 × H100 (primary inference for real-time summarization) + 2 × A10G for embeddings and async work. Expect effective steady-state sustained TPS ~120 if we parallelize across H100 instances and use batching for embeddings.
- Option B (cost-weighted): 2 × H100 + 6 × A10G with aggressive batching and prefix/KV caching. Slightly higher tail risk on very long requests but significantly lower monthly commit.

Concurrency & batching notes
- For 450 tokens avg, target request concurrency ~60–80 concurrent in-flight requests to maintain 120 TPS with reasonable batching windows (10–20ms batching).
- We recommend enabling KV/prefix caching for repeated context to reduce per-request tokens.

Bursting to Hosted API
- Yes, we can route overflow to Hosted for short bursts; operational caveats: (1) Hosted uses separate capacity and pricing; (2) fallbacks must be authorized in your routing policy to avoid data leaving your VPC — we can configure a sanitized fallback.

Next tactical steps
1) If you confirm which sizing option aligns with your tolerance (latency-first vs cost-weighted) we will produce a short one-page configuration + committed spend estimate for Purchasing.
2) We will schedule a 2-hour benchmark window where we run your sample payload over both H100 and A10G configurations and return latency/tokens/sec results.
3) Grace will prepare a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a templated procurement summary.

I've updated the attached worksheet with the two sizing options (redwood-dedicated-worksheet-v1.xlsx). Vivek and Grace — can you confirm whether we should include a 7-day pilot cost in the MAP?

Thanks — Jordan
